title.value: Coping With Simulators That Don’t Always Return
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning and throughout the paper.
title.quote: Coping With Simulators That Don’t Always Return

analysis.description: The paper addresses computational inefficiencies in deterministic simulators that don't return values for certain inputs due to state perturbations and proposes a method using conditional normalizing flows to improve computational efficiency by reducing simulator failures.

type.justification: The paper presents experiments and real-world applications such as with bouncing balls and robotics simulator MuJoCo to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed methods.
type.quote: We first demonstrate our approach on a toy problem...Our second example uses a simulator of balls bouncing elastically...We now apply our method to the popular robotics simulator MuJoCo [Todorov et al., 2012].

name.justification: The paper focuses significantly on tackling issues related to simulators that fail under certain conditions.
name.quote: We believe this work has readily transferable practical contributions to not just the machine learning community, but the wider scientific community where such naively modified simulation platforms are widely deployed.

name.justification: The paper proposes using Conditional Autoregressive Flow for learning state-dependent density of perturbations to improve simulator efficiencies.
name.quote: We train an autoregressive flow to fit this density (§3.3), and describe how this can be used in inference.
